_comment: What villagers say aloud as the heir walks past them (Barks, NPC.say). A few words, then they carry on. Like a conversation (data/dialogue.json), a remark never names a rank or a number: a gift shows only as a clue, the stronger the gift the more often the talk turns to it, and modesty or boasting bends how it sounds. Worries are real: someone only grumbles about hunger, crowding or overwork when it's true. {lord} = my lord / my lady, {title} = lord / lady, {site} = a building going up, {charter} = the settlement's charter.
_range: The heir must come within `range` paces to be remarked on, and go past `leave_range` before the same person speaks again.
_timing: Seconds of real time: no one speaks twice within `cooldown`, and no two remarks come within `gap` of each other.
_recent: A line isn't said again until this many others have been.
_moods: Opinion of the heir at or above `fond_at` is fond, at or below `sour_at` sour. The stores are lean below `lean_days` of food.

kin: There you are! Off on your rounds?
child: Mam says I have to bow to you.
guest: {lord}. Your village is lovelier than I was told.
My family speaks well of yours, {lord}.
I hope my visit pleases you, {lord}.

lord: Walk with me another time. I've petitions to hear.
Our neighbours watch us closely. Remember it.
lady: The household eats more than it earns, I swear it.
Mind your boots in the hall.
noble_scion: My tutor says I'll make a scholar yet.
dowager: In my day the hall was never this quiet.
Sit with me before the light goes.
housekeeper: Out from under my feet, the bread's rising.
Someone's tracked mud through my kitchen again.
knight: The lads are slow on the left today.
guard_captain: I'll have the watch doubled after dark.
soldier: Nothing on the road but carts and crows.
farmer: Rain or shine, the furrows won't wait.
farmhand: My back's not what it was.
miller: Mind the flour dust, {lord}. It gets everywhere.
baker: Ovens are hot. Stand back a pace.
blacksmith: Strike while it's hot, they say. They're right.
This iron's got a temper on it.
carpenter: Good seasoned timber. Hard to come by.
apprentice: I'll get it right this time. I will.
The master says my joints are crooked.
merchant: Fine cloth, {lord}, fresh from the coast!
Prices are up again. Blame the roads.
innkeeper: The ale's good today, {lord}. Better than yesterday's.
Another barrel to tap before the evening.
tavern_hand: Four tankards, two pies... or was it three pies?
priest: The roof leaks over the altar again.
herbalist: Mind where you tread, that's good sorrel.
stonecutter: Good stone rings true when you strike it.
Dust in my lungs, dust in my bread.
laborer: A day's work for a day's bread.
Whatever needs hauling, I'll haul it.
builder: Another course of stone by sundown.

leisure: A fine day to do nothing at all.
Have you heard the news from the mill?
A cup of ale and a bit of sun. That's all I ask.
play: I'm a knight! You be the dragon!
home: Off home. My feet are done in.

midday: Sun's high. Time for bread and cheese.
evening: Nearly done for the day, thank the saints.

Spring: Lambing season. No one's slept in a week.
Mud to the ankles. Good for the seed, though.
Summer: Hot enough to bake bread on the stones.
Haymaking soon. Pray it stays dry.
Autumn: The geese are leaving. Winter's on its way.
Winter: Bitter cold. My fingers have forgotten me.
Snow's coming. I can feel it in my knees.

hungry: The stores are bare, {lord}. The children cry for bread.
Nothing in the pot again tonight.
We can't work on empty bellies, {lord}.
overworked: I've not stopped since dawn. Nor yesterday.
Too much work, too few hands.
crowded: Too many of us under one roof.
We sleep three to a bed at home.
lonely: Nobody much to talk to, these days.
restless: There must be more to life than this.
Same work, every day. I could do so much more.
I wasn't made for this, {lord}. I know it.
mourning: Forgive me, {lord}. We buried someone dear not long ago.
The house is so quiet now.
I keep thinking I hear them at the door.
unhappy: Don't mind me. Just a bad day. A bad week.

happy: Life's good in this village. I'll say that.

family._comment: Life at home, offered only when it's true (Barks.pools_for).
baby: We've a new babe at home, {lord}! Not a wink of sleep.
Have you seen our little one? Strong lungs, that one.
A new mouth to feed, and worth every crumb.
children: My little ones keep me on my toes.
The children grow faster than the barley.

_worries: unhappy: happiness below 35; happy: above 78; restless: a gifted, ambitious person stuck in humble work (MoodSystem.wasted_talent_penalty).

leadership: Someone has to tell them what to do.
They'd listen if I spoke up. They always do.
If I don't sort this out, nobody will.
Folk follow me without my asking. Strange, that.
Put me in charge and you'd see this place run like a mill.
combat: I could take him at wrestling. Probably.
Feet apart, weight low. That's how you hold a staff.
Nobody in the lane can best me with a cudgel.
Three men jumped me on the road once. Once.
A blade sits in my hand like it was made for it.
intelligence: Why do the swallows leave, I wonder?
Now how does that work, exactly?
If the wheel turned the other way it'd grind faster. I'm sure of it.
I counted the stars last night. Then I counted them again.
I've worked out the moon's turnings on the barn door. All of them.
The priest's sums are wrong. I checked them thrice.
politics: Did you hear what the miller's wife said?
I could patch up that quarrel over the fence, if they'd let me.
The merchant always gives me his best price. I just smile.
Half the village owes me a favour. The other half doesn't know it yet.
I always know who's lying, {lord}. Always.
administration: Two sacks, three sacks... where's the fourth?
I know to the egg what every house has put by.
The steward's tallies are a mess. I could mend them.
I could tell you what every house owes, and to whom.
Give me the granary keys and nothing would go to waste. Nothing.
ambition: One day I'll have a cart of my own.
I won't be doing this forever. Mark me.
There's a world past those hills.
One day they'll sing about me, {lord}.
I'll have a hall of my own before I'm grey. You'll see.

leadership: I'm the leader of our gang!
Everyone plays my game, because it's the best.
combat: I beat Tom at wrestling. Twice!
Watch! I can hit that post from here!
intelligence: Why is the sky blue? Do you know?
I can read the signs on the inn. Ask me one!
politics: I know a secret about the miller!
If you give me a sweet I'll tell you who broke the cart.
administration: I've got eleven pebbles. I counted.
I keep all my treasures in a row.
ambition: When I grow up I'm going to be a knight!
I'm going to live in a castle one day.

building: All that hammering at the new {site}. Good work, though.
They say the {site} will be finished soon.
Have you seen the new {site} going up?
charter: A {charter} now, they say. Fancy that.
Folk come from all round since we got our charter.

eyed: There's something in your eye, {lord}. Like you're weighing me.
Folk say you see right through people.
You looked at me strangely the other day, {lord}.
